slides.title: First sounds and greetings
slides.slide: L1 Basic · First sounds and greetings
slides.notes: Say hello, give your name and name three everyday objects in Arabic. Notes: teach مرحبا (marhaba, hello) and كتاب (kitab, book) aloud before any writing; learners greet a partner and point to a book, a pen and a door while saying each word.

slides.title: Letters and the right-to-left page
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Letters and the right-to-left page
slides.notes: Recognise that Arabic is written right to left and copy the shapes of the first eight letters. Notes: show that letters change form at the start, middle and end of a word; learners trace the letter for b, then find it in three printed words.

slides.title: Simple sentences and a first reading
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Simple sentences and a first reading
slides.notes: Read and write short present-tense sentences about yourself, family and daily life with short vowels marked. Notes: use هذا كتاب (hadha kitab, this is a book) as the model; learners build five new sentences, swapping the noun each time, and read them aloud.

slides.title: Everyday conversation and roots
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Everyday conversation and roots
slides.notes: Hold a two-minute conversation on school, food and travel and use the three-letter root idea to guess new words. Notes: show k-t-b giving kitab (book) and katib (writer); learners find the root in four given words, then order a meal in a role-play.

slides.title: Formal Arabic and dialect awareness
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Formal Arabic and dialect awareness
slides.notes: Compare Modern Standard Arabic with one spoken dialect and write a formal letter of about 150 words. Notes: take one phrase, such as how to say 'how are you', in both registers; learners list three differences and choose the right register for a news item and a chat.

slides.title: Literary analysis and linguistics
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Literary analysis and linguistics
slides.notes: Analyse a classical or modern text for grammar, rhetoric and register, and write a reasoned essay in Arabic. Notes: choose a short poem of eight lines; learners mark case endings, name one image used, and explain in a 400-word essay how the form supports the meaning.

slides.title: Translation, research and teaching
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Translation, research and teaching
slides.notes: Design and defend a translation or research project that handles dialect variation, with a documented method. Notes: pick a 500-word article and translate it for two audiences; justify every choice about register, note untranslatable terms, and have a native reader check the result.
